page: Microsoft Azure D128ls_v7 is an x86_64 virtual machine instance within the Dlsv7 family, virtualized on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system incorporates an Intel processor delivering 128 dedicated vCPUs accompanied by 256.0 GB of RAM. The memory configuration provides exactly 2.0 GB per vCPU, forming a dense compute profile distinct from standard 1:4 memory configurations. The instance contains no integrated GPUs and does not provision onboard local storage, requiring persistent disk operations to use remote Premium Storage volumes.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio establishes D128ls_v7 as a lean, compute-oriented server. By omitting onboard ephemeral disks, the architecture prioritizes host flexibility and dedicated core assignment while eliminating unused local disk capacity. The primary operational tradeoff involves reliance on network-attached storage, which places all storage throughput and latency expectations onto remote storage interfaces. For environments where memory requirements scale moderately relative to thread counts, this design avoids the overhead of overprovisioned RAM.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the Dlsv7 configuration provides high processing capacity per unit of allocated resource by rightsizing memory allocation for CPU-bound tasks. Workloads that do not require high memory density avoid paying for unallocated RAM capacity across the 128 cores. The server is well suited for horizontally scaled computing tasks, high-concurrency batch processing, large-scale source code compilation, CI/CD orchestration, and general-purpose microservice architectures operating without large caching layers.
description: Microsoft Azure D128ls_v7 is an x86_64 compute-focused virtual machine instance built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization and powered by an Intel processor. The instance features 128 dedicated vCPUs alongside 256.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 2.0 GB per core. It operates without dedicated hardware accelerators, providing zero GPUs, and includes no local ephemeral storage, directing all disk I/O operations toward remote Premium Storage solutions. By reducing the per-core memory footprint relative to standard general-purpose offerings, the D128ls_v7 delivers an infrastructure profile optimized for compute density. This resource balance provides a cost-efficient hardware allocation for compute-dominant architectures where high per-core memory provisioning would remain underutilized. Best-fit deployments include distributed computing worker nodes, multi-threaded batch processing, software compilation pipelines, continuous integration runners, and parallel simulation tasks that require intensive multi-core processing without substantial memory overhead.
